Site of the Former Ketsch Synagogue

Synagogue site · Ketsch, Germany

From the mid-1820s, the small Jewish community of Ketsch, which also included Jewish residents of neighboring Brühl, held services in a synagogue established in a house on Hockenheimer Straße that was co-owned by a Jewish community member. The congregation, never numbering more than about 44 people, dissolved by the mid-1930s under Nazi persecution; thirteen Jewish residents born in Ketsch were later murdered in the Holocaust. The building continued to be used as a private residence after the community's end and remained standing until it was demolished in the 1990s. Two Stolpersteine (memorial stones) were placed nearby in 2016.
